styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small drawer-style med cart, roughly 12x16 px, so it is about one tile in size. It measures 13 visible tones per 16x16 tile, which is within the reference range (hedge 9, stall 17, well 20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so the drawer fronts, white top and stripes are broken up by highlights, edge lines and handle dots, with no 5x5 flat fills. Only 7% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline leans tinted (bluish or brownish dark tones) rather than the near-black sticker line, and the forms are separated partly by value. The main weakness is that each material (white body, blue drawer, red drawer) has only about 3-4 lightness steps against roughly 5-6 on the references, and it has less fine grain than the stall or well. Even so, it is no thinner or flatter than the hedge or bench references at this scale, and a careful artist would accept it next to them.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small, roughly one-tile cart with a white top and stacked blue and teal drawers. It reads clearly as a prop of the same kind as the references. On the measured facts it holds up: 13 visible tones per 16x16 tile, against 9 for the hedge, 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the roofed well. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. Only 7% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is tinted (dark blue-grey beside the drawers) and does not read as a black sticker line. The drawers and body show about 3-4 lightness steps each, with handle highlights and edge shading. That is a little below the 5-6 steps in the stronger Beodeul props, and the total palette of 17 colours is far smaller than the stall's 40. Per-tile richness is nonetheless in the range of the references, and the piece is not noticeably flatter or thinner than the hedge. I judge it a marginal pass, slightly lower in density than the best references but acceptable beside them.
